Nature of offence complained of 279/338 IPC & 3/181, 39/192 and 146/196 MV Act Plea of the accused person Not Guilty Date of reserving order 16.03.2023 Final Order Convicted under Section 279/338 IPC &

BRIEF STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE:-
1.

In the present case, accused Dilip is facing trial for offences punishable under Section 279/338 IPC & 3/181, 146/196/39/192 MV Act on the allegations that on 24.11.2011 at about 1.00 am in front of H. NO. 20 A, P.R. Road, within the jurisdiction of PS Tughlak Road falling within the jurisdiction of PS Tughlak Road,
accused was driving a car (Maruti Van bearing No. DL11LE-6376) rashly and negligently and while driving so, accused hit a vehicle on the rear side of DTC Bus bearing NO.
FIR No. 93/2011 PS Tuglak Road State vs. Dilip Page No. 1 of 9 DL-1PC-8565 resulting a grievous injuries to his co-passenger Ram Snehi.
2.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed on 08.02.2013 and cognizance was taken on same day.

Copy of charge sheet was also supplied to accused on the said date and notice for offences punishable U/s. 279/304A IPC was given to accused on 26.08.2013, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
3.
To prove its case, prosecution has examined seven witnesses.
4. PW1 Sh. Ram Snehi has deposed that he was coming after purchasing vegetables and other food material on the van and the van was driven by the accused.
The offending vehicle was driven by the accused in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner.
Due to high speed the vehicle which was driven by the accused collided with the bus standing at bus stand due to which the complainant and the accused got injured.
After that they have been taken to the hospital by the police officials.
PW1 has identified the accused.

1 5.

PW2 Sh. Ram Charan who has deposed that in the year 2011, he conducted mechanical inspection of a bus bearing registration no. DL 1PC 8565 at PS tughlak Road, Delhi and also prepared a report which is now Ex. PW-2/A. FIR No. 93/2011 PS Tuglak Road State vs. Dilip Page No. 2 of 9 6.
PW3 Sh. Anand Singh, who has deposed that on 24.11.2011, he was posted a a conductor in DTC bus bearing registration no. DL 1PC 8565.
he deposed that when the bus was halted at a bus stop in its box for boarding and de-boarding of the passengers, suddenly he heard a very load noise which came from the back side of the bus.

When he went to back side of the bus he saw that one van bearing registration no. DL 1LE 6376 of white colour was struck on the backside of the bus and its driver and passengers also got struck inside the van due to the impact.
Both the rescued from the van and were taken to the hospital with the help of public persons and both were taken to the hospital by PCR van.
The witness has failed to identify the accused as driver of the said van, rather he stated that the accused was sitting on the passenger side of the van.
7. PW4 is Sh. Parmod Kumar, who has deposed that on 24.11.2011, he was posted as a driver in a DTC bus bearing registration no. DL 1PC 8565.
He deposed that when the bus was halted at a bus stop in its box for boarding and de-boarding of the passengers, sunndely he heard a very load noise which came from the back side of the bus.

When he went to back side of the bus he saw that one van bearing registration no. DL 1LE 6376 of white colour was struck on the backside of the bus and its driver and passengers also got struck inside the van due to the impact.

Both the rescued from the van and were taken to the hospital with the help of public persons and both were taken to the FIR No. 93/2011 PS Tuglak Road State vs. Dilip Page No. 3 of 9 hospital by PCR van.
The witness has correctly identified the accused as a driver of the said van.

The bus was seized by the IO vide seizure memo Ex. PW1/B.
8.
PW5 is Ct. Anish who joined the investigation with IO/SI Gourav Gupta and accused namely Dilip Kumar was arrested from Gali no. 15, Khajoori Khas.

After interrogation, the accused was arrested by him vide arrest memo already Ex. PW-4/C.
9.

PW 6 is Sh. Arvinder Singh (Mechanical expert) who has deposed that he went to PS Tuglak Road,
where he met SI Gaurav Gupta.
The Maruti Van bearing No. DL 1LE 6376 which was shown by SI Gaurav Gupta.
10. PW 7 ASI Mahbir, has deposed that he was posted as Constable at PS Tuglak Road.
He alongwith IO SI Gaurav Gupta went to the spot.
They found one DTC bus bearing no. DL 1PC 8565 and one Maruti Van bearing no. DL 1 LE 6376 in accidental condition.
The injured/driver of Maruti Van and the other injured who was sitting next to the driver of the Maruti Van were already taken to RML hospital.
IO interrogated teh driver of the bus namely Parmod Kumar and conductor Anand Singh who were present at the spot.
IO left him at hte spot and went to RML hospital.
After some time, IO came back at the spot and handed over Tehrir to him.
After that he went to the police station for the registration of FIR and original rukka and the same handed over to the IO.
The driver of the offending vehicle identified by him.

The photographs of both the vehicles shown to the witness and the same were identified by him and same is Ex. A7.
11.

Vide separate statement under Section 294 Cr.P.C., accused admitted copy of FIR no. 93/2011 PS Tuglak Road, DD no. 7A dated 24.11.2011, MLC no. 196411/2011 prepared by Dr. Anand Vishal,
CMO, Dr. RML Hospital, opinion on MLC 196411/2011 prepared by Dr. Manish Rawat, R. Dr. RML Hospital, MLC no. 196406/2011 prepared by Dr. Ravinder Singh, CMO, Dr. RML Hospital,
Superdarinama of DTC Bus bearing registration number DL 1PC 8565, photographs of the spot taken by the Ct. Sandeep and consequential witnesses were dropped from examination.

Thereafter,
PE was closed.
12. Statement of accused was recorded U/Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. r/w Section 281 Cr.P.C. on 06.02.2023 wherein he denied the case of the prosecution and pleaded innocence.
Accused stated that he does not want to lead defence evidence.
13. Final arguments were advanced at length by Ld. APP for the State and counsel for accused.
14. I have considered the submissions and perused the record carefully.

15. This being a criminal case, the burden of proving guilt of accused lies upon the prosecution for which the standard required FIR No. 93/2011 PS Tuglak Road State vs. Dilip Page No. 5 of 9 is beyond reasonable doubt.

The ingredients required to prove offence punishable 279/338 IPC in this case are :
a. That the accused was driving the offending vehicle on a public place so rashly and negligently as to cause hurt to any person.
b. That accused got injured of victim due to his rash or negligent act.

16. Now let us examine if the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused for offence punishable under Section 279/338 IPC.
17.
The identity of the accused has never been in dispute during the trial.
PW1, who is the eye-witness of the accident as well as the injured, correctly identified the accused in the court.
Further, PW4 who was the driver of the DTC Bus and also an eye witness correctly identified the accused in Court.
In the statement of the accused recorded u/S. 313 Cr.P.C. on 06.02.2023, it has been admitted by the accused that he was driving the offending vehicle on the date of accident.
It has never been the case of the defence that the accused was in fact not the driver of the offending vehicle on the date of the accident.
It is therefore, beyond reasonable doubt that on the date of incident, the offending vehicle was being driven by the accused Dilip.

18. The only thing required to prove offence punishable under Section 279/338 IPC is that accused was driving the offending FIR No. 93/2011 PS Tuglak Road State vs. Dilip Page No. 6 of 9 vehicle rashly and negligently, which endangered human life and safety thereby causing grievous injury to State vs . Dilip on 29 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71614847/
3 the injured/victim.

In the present case, the eye witness PW1 has clearly deposed that the offending vehicle was being driven by the accused in rash and negligent manner at very high speed due to which the offending vehicle which was being driven by the accused collided with the bus standing at the bus stand.
Further, from the perusal of the site plan Ex. PW4/A, it is clear that the DTC bus was standing at the bus stand.
In the facts of the present case, the collision into the said DTC bus by the offending vehicle in itself shows that the latter was being driven in a rash and negligent manner.
Further, the witness PW-1 has also deposed that he had asked the accused to drive carefully before the accident occurred.
A perusal of mechanical inspection report shows that there are damages in the front bumper and front side body of the offending vehicle.
Further, perusal of the mechanical inspection report of the DTC bus shows that there is a damage on the rear side bumper of the said bus.
Both the reports support the testimony of PW1, PW3 and PW4 that the offending vehicle struck on the backside of the DTC Bus which had halted at the bus stand of Prithvi Raj Road.
All the above documents alongwith testimony of witnesses corroborate the version of the prosecution regarding rash and negligence on the part of the accused.

19. As far as the offence u/S. 338 IPC is concerned, the testimony of PW-1/injured and his MLC Ex.
A3 and the opinion on the same Ex. A4 (both admitted by the accused on FIR No. 93/2011 PS Tuglak Road State vs. Dilip Page No. 7 of 9 23.10.2019) reveal that the accused received grievous injuries.
The nature of injury therefore established and proved.
20. As already discussed above, the offending vehicle collided with the DTC Bus on its rear side (as per the testimony of PW1, PW3 and PW4).
It naturally leads to the conclusion that the offending vehicle had so much speed that it could not be controlled at the bus stand.
Such facts call for application of the doctrine of res ipsa loquiter i.e. the facts speaks for themselves.
Hence, on the basis of this doctrine, it is proved beyond reasonable that accused was driving the offending vehicle rashly and negligently, thus resulting in grievous injury of the victim.
21. The testimonies of PW1 & PW4 are consistent and cogent.
They have not been shaken in their respective cross-examinations and therefore, they are reliable witnesses inspiring the confidence of the court.
Further, the accused has not discharged his burden of proving the fact that on the day of the accident, the brakes of his vehicle failed as stated by him in his statement u/S. 313 Cr.P.C.
In fact, the mechanical inspection report Ex. PW6/A clearly states that there was no problem in the brakes of the offending vehicle DL1LE6376 (Maruti Van).

22. In view of the above, it stands proved that accused was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident, at the spot of the accident and that grievous injury was caused due to rash and negligent driving on the basis of doctrine of res ipsa loquiter.
FIR No. 93/2011 PS Tuglak Road State vs. Dilip Page No. 8 of 9

4 23.

Thus, as a cumulative effect of all the points discussed above, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt against accused and accordingly he is convicted for offence punishable u/s 279/338 IPC.
24.

The accused was also charged with the offence punishable u/S. 3/181, 39/192 and 146/196 MV Act, 1988 on the charges that he was not having a valid license, RC and Insurance of the offending vehicle bearing no. DL1LE 6376 on the date of the accident.
The accused has not brought on record any of the said documents during investigation or the course of trial.

He is therefore, accordingly,
convicted for the offences punishable u/S. 3/181, 39/192 and 146/196 MV Act.
Copy of this judgment be given free of cost to accused.

29.03.2023 )
